dedupe_keys.name: pamso parametric autotuning multi time scale optimization algorithm

description: PAMSO is an algorithm for solving large optimisation models with decisions on several time scales, such as integrated planning and scheduling. It tunes parameters in a low-fidelity model that represent its mismatch with a higher-fidelity model, treating the multi-scale cost as a black-box function optimised with derivative-free methods, and the tuned parameters can be transferred to similar problems. It was developed by Asha Ramanujam and Can Li and posted on arXiv on 23 July 2024; the abstract page does not name their institution. Case studies cover an integrated design and scheduling model with about 67,000 variables and a planning and scheduling model of electrified chemical plants with renewable power, with about 26 million variables. The preprint is available free online as a PDF; no code link or licence is stated on the abstract page. Caveats: it is a preprint method, not packaged software, and performance depends on the choice of low-fidelity model and tuning method. For simulation it makes very large capacity planning and scheduling problems for chemical plants tied to variable renewable supply tractable, useful for studies of industrial electrification and energy system resilience. It is related to the Aspen Plant Scheduler record in this catalogue, a commercial scheduling tool for the same plants.
